subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu direct session can become unusable after /reset or /new and fall back to generic 'Something went wrong...' while session index points to missing transcript IDs

question: Should text-command /new and /reset for direct chat sessions transactionally create or prewarm a durable transcript before the session family advances, or should recovery remain a doctor/next-turn repair behavior?
rationale: Current main has both transactional-style helpers and delayed transcript creation paths; choosing where reset/new durability belongs affects session storage semantics, user-visible recovery copy, and Feishu-specific doctor behavior.

options.title: Make reset/new durable before publish
options.body: Require the direct text-command reset/new path to create or prewarm the new transcript before persisting the new session id or usage-family membership, and fall back to the previous valid entry on failure.

options.title: Keep runtime behavior, strengthen repair
options.body: Leave reset/new acknowledgement behavior mostly unchanged but expand doctor/runtime repair to remove or remap orphaned usage-family ids and show a specific recovery message.

options.title: Fold into the broader Feishu UX issue
options.body: Track only the user-facing generic failure copy under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89247, accepting that this issue's session-family durability evidence remains separate.

recommendation.title: Make reset/new durable before publish
recommendation.body: Require the direct text-command reset/new path to create or prewarm the new transcript before persisting the new session id or usage-family membership, and fall back to the previous valid entry on failure.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about broad reset/new semantics in the auto-reply session path, where recent adjacent maintenance appears in local history.
